title: Sundarbans: Three Nights on the Mangrove Rivers
summary: A licensed vessel, an approved forest route and three nights between Katka, Haringata and Dublar Char - deer at dusk, kingfishers at first light, and Bagerhat’s Sixty Dome Mosque on the way in.

itinerary.title: 1 — Khulna to Noapara, first boat day
itinerary.detail: Pick-up at Khulna railway station or your hotel, brief safety and permit check at the Noapara counter, board the licensed vessel, sail the Shibsa to Katka. Evening walk on the estuarine beach; forest-registered guide on board throughout.

itinerary.title: 2 — Katka to Haringata
itinerary.detail: Sunrise from the Katka watchtower, then a small-boat push into the narrow creeks where the banks close in. Afternoon at Haringata’s deer breeding area, and a late-afternoon char walk for spotted deer and wild boar tracks. No night spotlighting: it is prohibited and we do not arrange it.

itinerary.title: 3 — Dublar Char day
itinerary.detail: Cross to Dublar Char, the big sandbank with its seasonal fishing camp, oyster beds and gharial banking area. Swim only where the crew choose the sandbar; lunch on board; return sail at golden hour.

itinerary.title: 4 — Mongla, Bagerhat and the drive back
itinerary.detail: Disembark at Mongla, visit the Sixty Dome Mosque and the Bagerhat mosque-city lane walk with an archaeology-trained guide, then transfer to Khulna or Dhaka. Add a night in Khulna if you would rather not drive on.

included: Forest-department permit filing and entry fees
Licensed cabin cruiser or mining boat, shared twin cabin with attached bath
All meals on board (Bangla, vegetarian available)
Khulna hotel on night 1 and airport/rail transfers
Fuel, driver allowance, and one bottled-water refill station per port
excluded: Soft drinks and laundry on board

title: Sundarbans Day Run from Khulna
summary: For travellers with one day and a real wish to see mangrove forest: dawn boat from Noapara, two creeks, a watchtower, lunch on board, back by late afternoon.

itinerary.title: 1 — Full day on the Shibsa
itinerary.detail: 06:00 pick-up in Khulna, 07:00 boat departure, creek navigation while the banks are still active with kingfishers and mudskippers, watchtower climb at Katka, rice and fish lunch on board, afternoon return via the shrimp-pond fringe. 17:00 drop-off. Boat capacity and permit counters close at dusk, so the schedule is fixed.

title: Cox’s Bazar, Himchari, Inani & Teknaf
summary: The 120 km beach done properly: midweek slots, sunrise at Himchari’s waterfall and temple, Inani’s low-tide rock shelves, then the boat to St. Martin’s if the weather window holds.

itinerary.title: 1 — Arrive, Sugandha point and the laboni swing
itinerary.detail: Flight or night-bus arrival, check in at Laboni/Kolatoli, late-afternoon walk to Sugandha where the beach narrows against the hill, seafood market briefing (buy at the counter, have it cooked, agree the price first).

itinerary.title: 2 — Himchari and Khuni Khular Pukhur
itinerary.detail: Early start up the ridge: Himchari waterfall (seasonal), the hill-top temple, and the hidden lagoon of Khuni Khular Pukhur behind the dunes. Macaque etiquette is covered on the way in - no food in hand, no plastic bags.

itinerary.title: 3 — Inani morning, Teknaf afternoon
itinerary.detail: Low tide at Inani for the rock shelves and black coral fragments exposed on the reef flat (walk in shoes, do not break or take any). Afternoon in Teknaf: the twin-ridge viewpoint, the Birmindia border marker view, and the sunset boat.

itinerary.title: 4 — Departure, or extend to St. Martin’s
itinerary.detail: Morning free for the beach, then transfer out. Guests adding St. Martin’s take the 09:00 launch from Teknaf and rejoin the return schedule two nights later.

included: Three nights beachfront hotel (standard or twin sharing)
Private AC vehicle with driver for all sightseeing
Entry fees for Himchari and the lagoon area
excluded: Launch tickets to St. Martin’s (Tk 2,200 return, weather-dependent)

title: St. Martin’s Island Weekend
summary: Two nights on the coral island with a timed landing at Chhera, a cycle round the main road, and the rules that keep the reef intact - which also explains why the season is only October to May.

itinerary.title: 1 — Teknaf to the island
itinerary.detail: Morning assembly at Teknaf jetty, 09:00 launch crossing (about 1 h 40 m), check-in at the resort or guesthouse block, evening on the east beach where the sand is still white after the day-trippers leave.

itinerary.title: 2 — Chhera at low tide, island by bicycle
itinerary.detail: Boat to Chhera timed to the published low water so the coral shelf is exposed for a short, shoe-on snorkel and nothing is touched or lifted. Return to Martin’s for an afternoon cycling the single road: coconut groves, the small Hindu temple at Uttar para, the mangrove fringe at the south end.

itinerary.title: 3 — Island morning and return launch
itinerary.detail: Sunrise on the west sand - the quiet side, where the overnight tide has laid down a fresh shelf and nobody is standing on it yet. Breakfast at 08:00, rooms vacated by 09:30, the 11:00 launch back to Teknaf, then the transfer to Cox’s Bazar airport or the night bus to Dhaka. If the launch is cancelled for weather the day becomes a coast-road return and we hold the hotel either way.

included: Return launch Teknaf-Martin’s with reserved seats
Chhera boat with timed landing permit
excluded: Scuba or glass-bottom boat (we do not sell reef-contact activities)
Plastic-bottled water on the island (refill points listed on arrival)

title: The North Bengal Heritage Loop: Paharpur to Puthia
summary: Somapura Mahavihara, Mahasthangarh, Kantajiu, Puthia, Bagha and Choto Sona in one arc with an archaeology-trained guide, terracotta at raking light, and the Varendra Museum when it is closed to everyone else.

itinerary.title: 1 — Rajshahi, Varendra and Godagari ghat
itinerary.detail: Arrive Rajshahi, morning at the Varendra Research Museum (the finest assemblage of Bengal sculpture outside Dhaka), late-afternoon at Godagari on the Padma, mango in season.

itinerary.title: 2 — Mahasthangarh and Kantajiu
itinerary.detail: Full day at the fortified city: the Jahajghata tank, Deva Angana, the site museum, then the drive north to Kantajiu for one of Bengal’s densest surviving terracotta fronts - best in the last hour of light.

itinerary.title: 3 — Paharpur and Dinajpur
itinerary.detail: Sunrise at Somapura Mahavihara before the coaches, the Bhutura monastery mound and the on-site museum, then Dinajpur for the Rajbari and the night at Shilsha Heritage Resort.

itinerary.title: 4 — Puthia and Bagha
itinerary.detail: The Puthia temple complex - Shyamakunda, Govinda, Keshor - then Bagha Mosque in the shallow forest depression where the acoustics carry, and the short run to the Adina site and Choto Sona Mosque at Gaur.

itinerary.title: 5 — Return via Natore
itinerary.detail: Early start for Natore: the Rajbari complex with its temple and the boat-shaped palace on the lake, then Chandan Ghur’s palace mound - a ruin now, but the terracotta panels and the moated layout show why the Rajputani families built here. Drop at Rajshahi airport or the intercity bus by 15:00, with time for a last plate of mango in season.

included: Four nights in heritage/tourist-circuit hotels (double sharing)
Private AC vehicle with driver for five days
ASI/DoA tickets at all listed sites
Museum guided sessions at Varendra and Paharpur
excluded: Rail or air tickets into/out of Rajshahi
Drone permits (not granted at protected sites)

title: Bagerhat Mosque City & the Forest Edge
summary: One of the finest concentrations of sultanate architecture on earth, plus the Sundarban fringe at Dublar Char road and the Shyamnagar village tracks that most visitors never see.

itinerary.title: 1 — Khulna museum, then the mosque city
itinerary.detail: Morning at the Khulna Divisional Museum for the river-boat models and the forest ethnography, drive to Bagerhat for the Sixty Dome Mosque at its best in the afternoon, the Khana and Mughal mosques, the tomb of Khan Jahan, and the tank walk. Night in Bagerhat or back to Khulna.

itinerary.title: 2 — Forest edge and char villages
itinerary.detail: The Rampal road to the forest-edge villages: timber boats at the ghat, honey-collector stalls, and the Shyamnagar embankment walk with dolphins in the Rupsa if the tide is right (never promised). Drop at Khulna by 15:00.

included: Guided mosque-city walk with a local historian
Boat hour on the Rupsa fringe

title: Srimangal Tea Gardens, Lawachara & Madhabkunda
summary: Cycle the estate roads before the plucking shift, walk Lawachara’s canopy boardwalk with a tribal guide, then the long walk in to Madhabkunda for the swim under the fall.

itinerary.title: 1 — Sylhet to the tea belt
itinerary.detail: Arrive Osmani International, transfer to Srimangal. Late-afternoon at the Narayana Tea Estate factory floor (when the rollers run) and the estate bazaar, tea at the manager’s cottage view point.

itinerary.title: 2 — Lawachara with a Kuki guide
itinerary.detail: Pre-dawn gibbon call walk, the canopy platform and the cave trail with a community guide from the Baghaiya/Halang cardamom gardens. Afternoon: the Madhabkunda long walk in, night at the forest gate.

itinerary.title: 3 — Madhabkunda falls and Bishnakand
itinerary.detail: Swim under the fall before the day trippers arrive, then the Shilpara Road to Bishnakand’s hilltop Shiva temple and the tea-mountain viewpoint above it.

itinerary.title: 4 — Sylhet: dargah, basket markets, departure
itinerary.detail: Return to Sylhet for Shah Jalal’s dargah before Friday prayer crowd, the bamboo and cane market, and drop at the airport or the night bus.

included: Three nights (two in Srimangal estate rest house class, one near Madhabkunda)
Community forest guide at Lawachara (fee supports the village committee)
Cycle hire for the estate loop
All entry fees and camera charges
excluded: Elephant or boat "experiences" that handle wildlife (not offered)

title: Sylhet’s Haor Waterworld in Monsoon
summary: When the haors fill, the roads become channels and the villages sit on islands. Row-boat between Tangaur, Bazaratung and Goylaghat, sleep on the embankment, and be honest: this is a wet, slow, wonderful season.

itinerary.title: 1 — Sunamganj and the Bazaratung boat
itinerary.detail: Transfer from Sylhet, afternoon row-boating through the flooded rice fields of Bazaratung while families move the last boro paddy, evening on the haor shore at Jagannath temple.

itinerary.title: 2 — Tangaur
itinerary.detail: Full day on Tangaur: the haor’s island villages, the 400 km view across water to the Garo hills, and the birding list that peaks in the wet months. Night at the Dakua camp on raised ground.

itinerary.title: 3 — Goylaghat and the Jaintia run-up
itinerary.detail: Morning boat back to Goylaghat, then the short climb on to the pine ridge above the haor, where on a clear day the whole water body reads as a sea with islands in it. The Jaintiapur border bazaar is the last stop - Khasi hill town, oranges in winter - then the drive back through Sunamganj to Sylhet, arriving around 18:00.

included: All boat hiring including the country-boat day on Tangaur
excluded: Hotel upgrades when properties close for flood (substitutions apply)
Boat-swim sessions if the water is unsafe

title: Bandarban, Rangamati & the Chandraket Ridge
summary: Three hills in five days: the twin-lake viewpoint and Roangchari sunrise, the Chandraket cloud line, and Rangamati’s hanging bridge - with community protocols respected and permits filed where required.

itinerary.title: 1 — Chattogram to Bandarban
itinerary.detail: Drive up the Kaptai road, ferry or road around the lake, evening in the Sangu valley town. Register at the deputy commissioner’s office for foreign guests if required for the route.

itinerary.title: 2 — Banai and the painted village
itinerary.detail: Trek in to Banai through betel-leaf gardens, the Chakma mural houses, lunch in the village, back for the Nilgiri sunset on the ridgeline.

itinerary.title: 3 — Chandraket
itinerary.detail: The 2,000 ft sandstone shelf at first light, with the plains and the Bay in the same frame. The trail is exposed; we walk it in dry conditions only, and turn back if the cloud closes.

itinerary.title: 4 — Tungichhara to Rangamati
itinerary.detail: Descend via the Sangu cascade route to the river crossing, then Rangamati: the hanging bridge, the Bajra Kurti viewpoint and the Chakma Rajapara museum.

itinerary.title: 5 — Kaptai and Boga Lake
itinerary.detail: Optional long day to Boga Lake and Tingi for the waterfall swim if the track is dry, or the Kaptai circuit with the Submerging Forest viewpoint; evening transfer to Chattogram.

included: Four nights: two guesthouse, one cottage, one lakeside hotel
All breakfasts and dinners, three packed lunches
Tribal community guide (fee paid to the co-operative)
Permit filing assistance and all village entry fees
excluded: Any activity in restricted upazilas where rules change at short notice

title: Padma Ghats: Godagari, Daulatdia & the Char Sandboxes
summary: Two days on the greatest river in Bengal: the ferry crossings, the char schools on sand, and the mango orchards of Rajshahi in the fruit season.

itinerary.title: 1 — Godagari to the char
itinerary.detail: Morning drive to Godagari ghat, country boat across to a char for the school built on sand, the fishing parasols at noon, and tea with the ferry crew while the current moves the islands. Night in Rajshahi.

itinerary.title: 2 — Mango, museum, and the great ferry
itinerary.detail: Seasonal orchard walk and the Varendra Museum, then the drive south to Daulatdia for one of the longest passenger ferry crossings in Asia, with Moheshwari’s island shrine in mid-river. Drop at Dhaka by night.

excluded: Season: ferry routes close in high flood (Jul-Sep) - date changes free

title: Barishal Char Life: Banaripara, Monpura & the Floating Market
summary: Homestay nights on chars that did not exist a generation ago: Banaripara’s eco-village, the Atghar-Kuriana floating market at dawn, Monpura’s long empty beach, and the mangrove nurseries replanting the erosion line.

itinerary.title: 1 — Barishal to Banaripara
itinerary.detail: Riverfront museum and the port-side breakfast, drive to the eco-village at Banaripara: community-managed homestay, bamboo craft and honey houses, mangrove nursery walk with the women’s planting committee.

itinerary.title: 2 — Floating market dawn, then the boat to Monpura
itinerary.detail: Up at 04:30 for the Atghar-Kuriana floating market where the boats sell vegetables and fish before sunrise, then the launch to Gaoria and the char-hop over to Monpura. Late afternoon on 10 km of sand with nobody on it.

itinerary.title: 3 — Monpura morning and return
itinerary.detail: Sunrise walk to the old lighthouse mound and the crab-farm channels, boat back to the mainland, drop at Barishal by 14:00 (or extend to Kuakata for a further night).

included: Two nights: one community homestay, one char resort
Breakfast, lunch on the market morning, all dinners
Homestay and guide fees paid locally
Mangrove nursery contribution (Tk 300 per guest, planted in your name)
excluded: Ferries to/from Barishal if arriving by road from Dhaka

title: Old Dhaka on Foot: Sadarghat to Lalbagh
summary: The working port, the Mughal palace, the kumortoli mask lanes and the best two hours of food in the country - with a rickshaw, a launch ride on the Buriganga and a curator at Ahsan Manzil who will actually open the storerooms.

itinerary.title: 1 — River, palace, mask lanes
itinerary.detail: Start at Sadarghat at 08:00 when the launch jetties are busiest, cross to Ahsan Manzil for the Nawab’s durbar halls, then walk old Dhaka’s kumortoli and the Armenian church lane. Afternoon at Islami Art Museum’s terracotta gallery, evening at Buriganga ghat for the ferry lights.

itinerary.title: 2 — Mughal fort to modernist capital
itinerary.detail: Lalbagh Fort at opening (the garden light is the reason), then Shahbagh: Curzon Hall, the university museum, the National Museum’s War of Liberation floor, and the Louis Kahn parliament complex at dusk from the outside. Baitul Mukarram for the last prayer light.

included: One night in a central hotel with breakfast
Rickshaw and launch rides as listed
All monument and museum tickets, curator-led access at Ahsan Manzil
excluded: Friday closures: Lalbagh is open, museums are not - itinerary is reversed
Lunches (we book the biryani and pitha stops)

title: Mymensingh: Zainul Abedin, Folk Art & the Jaintia Hills
summary: The famine sketches at the Zainul Abedin Museum, a Garo hill morning at China Clay Hills and Muktagachha’s zamindan houses, then Ratargul at dusk when the swimming logs start moving.

itinerary.title: 1 — Mymensingh gallery walk
itinerary.detail: Zainul Abedin Museum and the Dakurghat Bangla Academy campus along the river, Nazrul Academy at Churalia, evening on the Brammaputra-administration ghat.

itinerary.title: 2 — Zamindan palaces and the Garo hills
itinerary.detail: Muktagachha’s Rajbari cluster and Tongoor, then the Garo belt: China Clay Hills, the Tantipara waterfall, and a night at Shashi Lodge in the pine and rubber plantations.

itinerary.title: 3 — Ratargul before the crowds
itinerary.detail: An early boat into the swamp forest at Godhagari ghat, where the trunks stand in black water and the only sound is the oar; the mist and the kingfishers are both gone by 09:30. Then Talonga zamindan bari and its tank, a stop for bamboo craft on the highway, and the drive back to Mymensingh, Dhaka or Sylhet by evening.

included: Two nights with breakfast (one town hotel, one plantation lodge)
Boat at Ratargul with life jackets

title: Kuakata & the Pashur Coast
summary: A 32 km beach that faces both ways - sunrise and sunset on the same sand - with the Sonadia turtle-feeding grounds at low tide, Dubla char by boat, and the Pashur mouth where the delta lets go.

itinerary.title: 1 — Down the coast road
itinerary.detail: Khulna to Kuakata via Morrellganj and the Pashur mouth, stop at Kalapara for the beach-road crossing, sunset from the Rupakkari viewpoint.

itinerary.title: 2 — Chars, turtles and the market
itinerary.detail: Boat to Dubla and Sonadia at low tide (turtle-feeding grounds - keep 10 m from any animal, no torches, no flash), morning at the Kuakata fish market and the bamboo grove, afternoon at the Mangrove-belt nursery.

itinerary.title: 3 — Return via Laboni
itinerary.detail: Sunrise on the east end of the beach, then back through Laboni-Sugandha point for the picture everyone takes, drop at Khulna or Dhaka.

included: Two nights beachside hotel, breakfast included
Boat hire for the char day
